text:
{
  "summary": "The air quality in Delhi is currently Moderate, with an AQI of 195, measured at Talkatora Garden, Delhi - DPCC at 18:00 IST on 22 Nov. The dominant pollutant is PM2.5 at 89 µg/m³. Given that you have a child, it's important to take precautions to minimize exposure to this pollution.",
  "routines": [
    {
      "action": "Schedule outdoor errands, walks and exercise for 14:00–17:00; avoid 08:00–11:00.",
      "why": "Right now PM2.5 is 89 µg/m³ (AQI 195, Moderate) at Talkatora Garden, Delhi - DPCC. Smoke builds up when the air near the ground stops mixing, and clears when it mixes again. Your 09:00 start falls in the station's dirtiest window, and because you have a child, minimizing their exposure during peak pollution times is crucial.",
      "impact": "62% less PM2.5: over the last 24 h this station averaged 84 µg/m³ during 14:00–17:00 vs 221 µg/m³ during 08:00–11:00.",
      "personalizedFor": "Because of your child",
      "priority": "medium",
      "factId": "outdoor_timing"
    },
    {
      "action": "Move workouts and children's active play indoors until AQI improves.",
      "why": "Exercise makes you breathe deeper and faster while PM2.5 is 89 µg/m³ (AQI 195, Moderate) at Talkatora Garden, Delhi - DPCC. Since you have a child, it's important to protect them from inhaling more pollutants during active play.",
      "impact": "Moderate exercise inhales about 6.2× more air than sitting (US EPA Exposure Factors Handbook), so indoor exercise avoids most of that extra dose.",
      "personalizedFor": "Because of your child",
      "priority": "medium",
      "factId": "exercise_indoors"
    },
    {
      "action": "Take the metro instead of car for your 12 km commute.",
      "why": "Enclosed metro travel had the lowest in-transit PM2.5 in Delhi measurements (Goel et al. 2015), which is a better option for your daily commute to reduce your exposure.",
      "impact": "About 55% less PM2.5 inhaled per trip.",
      "personalizedFor": "Your daily commute",
      "priority": "medium",
      "factId": "commute_exposure"
    }
  ],
  "indoor": [
    {
      "action": "Build a DIY purifier: a box fan with four MERV-13 filters taped into a cube (about ₹3,000).",
      "why": "Indian homes are leaky, so indoor PM2.5 tracks outdoor levels unless air is filtered. Building a DIY purifier is a budget-friendly way to protect your child from indoor air pollution.",
      "impact": "Cuts bedroom PM2.5 by about 82% at steady state (mass-balance model, 36 m³ room, windows shut).",
      "personalizedFor": "Because of your child",
      "priority": "high",
      "factId": "purifier"
    },
    {
      "action": "Air out rooms for 10–15 minutes during 14:00–17:00; keep windows shut otherwise.",
      "why": "You still need fresh air for CO₂ and humidity; timing it to the cleanest hours limits what comes in, which is important for your home's air quality.",
      "impact": "Lets in about 62% less PM2.5 than airing out during 08:00–11:00 (this station, last 24 h).",
      "personalizedFor": "Your home",
      "priority": "medium",
      "factId": "ventilation_timing"
    },
    {
      "action": "Run the chimney/exhaust on high while cooking, use lids, and prefer back burners; avoid deep-frying with the house sealed.",
      "why": "Frying and tadka create indoor PM2.5 spikes that can exceed outdoor smog. Since you have a child, reducing these indoor sources is important for their health.",
      "impact": "Hoods moving ≥ 200 cfm capture over 75% of cooking particles on front burners, more on back burners (Singer et al. 2012).",
      "personalizedFor": "Because of your child",
      "priority": "medium",
      "factId": "cooking_exhaust"
    },
    {
      "action": "Skip mosquito coils, incense and dhoop indoors; use mesh screens or electric repellents.",
      "why": "Burning anything indoors adds smoke on top of the outdoor smog you are trying to keep out. This is especially important because you have a child, and their lungs are more vulnerable to smoke.",
      "impact": "One mosquito coil releases as much PM2.5 as 75–137 cigarettes (Liu et al. 2003).",
      "personalizedFor": "Because of your child",
      "priority": "high",
      "factId": "no_indoor_smoke"
    },
    {
      "action": "Keep houseplants for wellbeing, but don't rely on them to clean the air.",
      "why": "The popular 'air-purifying plants' claim comes from sealed-chamber tests that don't scale to homes, so while they can be good for your home's aesthetic, they won't significantly improve air quality.",
      "impact": "Negligible: you would need 100–1000 plants per m² to match normal ventilation (Cummings & Waring 2020).",
      "personalizedFor": "Your home",
      "priority": "low",
      "factId": "plants_reality"
    }
  ],
  "alternatives": [
    {
      "action": "Commute by metro instead of car.",
      "why": "Vehicle exhaust is a major share of winter PM2.5 and NO₂ in Indian cities; shared transport cuts both per person, making it a better choice for your 12 km commute.",
      "impact": "Saves about 13.8 kg CO₂ a week (718 kg a year).",
      "personalizedFor": "Your 12 km commute",
      "priority": "high",
      "factId": "transit_switch"
    },
    {
      "action": "Carpool with one colleague or neighbour on days you must drive.",
      "why": "Two people in one car halves the exhaust per person on the same road, which helps reduce emissions for your 12 km drive.",
      "impact": "Saves about 7.8 kg CO₂ a week for you (406 kg a year).",
      "personalizedFor": "Your 12 km drive",
      "priority": "medium",
      "factId": "carpool"
    },
    {
      "action": "Ask to work from home on the worst smog days (AQI 301 or higher).",
      "why": "Each skipped commute removes both your exhaust and your exposure for the day, which can benefit your health given your work schedule.",
      "impact": "One day a week saves about 3.1 kg CO₂ (162 kg a year) and two trips of exposure.",
      "personalizedFor": "Your work schedule",
      "priority": "low",
      "factId": "wfh_day"
    },
    {
      "action": "Compost leaves and garden waste instead of burning; report open burning on the CPCB Sameer app.",
      "why": "Open burning of biomass and garbage is a major winter PM2.5 source in north India, and avoiding it helps improve the air quality in your neighbourhood.",
      "impact": "Every 10 kg not burned avoids about 63 g of PM2.5 (Akagi et al. 2011).",
      "personalizedFor": "Your neighbourhood",
      "priority": "medium",
      "factId": "no_burning"
    }
  ]
}
